title: RBAC v2: permission assertion lab and conformance suite
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Purpose: Build a deterministic, repeatable test harness (the Permission Assertion Lab) that exercises RBAC v2 guardrails across the service surface: token-based API gates, admin console flows, and SAML/SSO-initiated sessions. The harness will generate canonical permission matrices and mutated variants, run them through the authorization engine, collect audit logs, and assert conformance against an authoritative policy oracle. Scope: tests for positive/negative permission assertions for API routes, resource-level scoping, escalation paths (role inheritance), admin-only controls, and SSO mapping (SAML group -> role). Output: concise failure diffs, a flakiness score per test, and automated repair suggestions (e.g., missing deny rules, incorrect group mappings). Acceptance criteria: (1) CI job that runs the core suite on every RBAC-related PR and fails if a regression is detected; (2) A set of ~250 canonical fixtures covering typical enterprise roles, edge cases, and known historical regressions; (3) Audit log parity checks that guarantee that every evaluated decision emits the expected structured log fields; (4) SSO test harness that validates assertion attributes when simulating an IdP-authenticated session. Integration points: integrates with the auth service test harness, the console e2e suite, and the centralized log collector (splunk/kinesis). Deliverables: test harness code, fixtures, pipeline job (ci/rbac-conformance), and an initial dashboard for weekly flakiness and regression metrics. Rollout: start as a nightly job for the first two weeks, then gate to PR-level runs once flakiness < 1%.
